decisions.quote:
In the eighth installment of
Data Replicada
, we report our attempt to replicate a recently published
Journal of Marketing Research
(JMR) article entitled, “The Left-Digit Bias: When and Why Are Consumers Penny Wise and Pound Foolish?” (
.htm
).
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this request. The source text reports two pre-registered MTurk replications (N = 1,099 and N = 1,555) retesting Study 1 (N = 145) of the Journal of Marketing Research article 'The Left-Digit Bias: When and Why Are Consumers Penny Wise and Pound Foolish?'. Crossref metadata for shipped row input_row_index 2723 (DOI 10.1177/0022243720932532, Sokolova, Seenivasan, & Thomas, 2020) confirms that it is this exact Journal of Marketing Research article. The blind target left authors, year, and DOI blank only because the blog post text names the article by title and journal without printing a formal bibliographic entry. Target 0 is already represented by shipped row 2723.

decisions.quote: Terman’s study was the first to systematically document the lives of the intellectually gifted. This cross-sectional study replicates and extends some of Terman’s findings on characteristics of the gifted in childhood
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this request. Only the abstract is available in the supplied source text, and it states that the study replicates and extends some of Terman's findings on characteristics of the gifted in childhood without providing an in-text citation, publication year, title, or reference list entry. While shipped row input_row_index 138 (Terman, 1926, 'Genetic studies of genius') is a plausible match, the abstract alone does not settle whether the specific cited target publication is Terman (1926) or another volume/report of Terman's giftedness research.

corrected_value.authors: Alesina, Alberto, Miano, Armando and Stantcheva, Stefanie
corrected_value.title: Immigration and redistribution.

decisions.location: Section 3 Data and Research Design, p. 7; Section 4.2, pp. 12-14; References, p. 20
decisions.quote:
Our pre-registered (see Appendix B.1 for blinded version) survey design builds
upon and replicates Magni (2021) and Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023)
with a quota-representative (age, gender, education, region) sample of the sur-
vey company Kantar.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this request. The paper conducts a pre-registered survey experiment in Germany (N = 1,587) that explicitly retests two distinct published priming studies: Magni (2021) (sibling target_index 0, which matches shipped row input_row_index 2261, DOI 10.1017/s0007123420000046, published online in 2020 and in print in 2021 in the British Journal of Political Science) and Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023) (target_index 1, 'Immigration and redistribution.', The Review of Economic Studies 90(1):1-39; no DOI is printed in the source text). In Section 4.2 (Figure 4, Models 1-5), the authors empirically retest the immigration priming treatment and causal chain of Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023), comparing their null effect of immigration priming on overall redistribution support and negative effect on welfare chauvinism against the original study's finding that immigration priming reduces support for redistribution. Shipped row 2261 represents only Magni (2020/2021), an independent study by a different author on inequality priming in Italy; report equivalence does not apply, so Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023) is a genuinely missing original target.

decisions.quote: The optimal cut-off scores identified in the current study reflect the same results configured by the prior study. LAY SUMMARY: ADOS-2 Toddler Module has been widely used for the ASD assessment, but there have been limited research on its clinical validity. This study is the first replication of the ADOS-2 Toddler Module with a large independent sample. We examined alignment of the ADOS-2 Toddler Module classification with clinicians' determination of ASD, with assessing cut-off scores, and confirmed the clinical validity of ADOS-2 Toddler Module. Cut-off scores of ADOS-2 Toddler Module cited in the manual yielded best clinical utility for diagnosing ASD in toddlers.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this request. The article body is unavailable; the source text contains only the abstract, lay summary, and a single reference-list excerpt for Luyster et al. (2009) (DOI 10.1007/s10803-009-0746-z). While the abstract states that the optimal cut-off scores reflect 'the same results configured by the prior study', the lay summary states that 'Cut-off scores of ADOS-2 Toddler Module cited in the manual yielded best clinical utility for diagnosing ASD in toddlers', which corresponds to shipped row input_row_index 143 (Lord et al., 2012, 'Autism diagnostic observation schedule--2nd edition (ADOS-2)'). Without the article body, the available evidence does not settle whether 'the prior study' refers to Luyster et al. (2009) or whether Luyster et al. (2009) and the ADOS-2 manual in shipped row 143 represent alternate reports of the same Toddler Module cut-off configuration rather than an omitted independent original study.

decisions.location: Abstract, p. 187; Introduction, p. 188; Table 1, p. 193; Conclusions, p. 204
decisions.quote:
In the original study, 
Shelton-Strong and Mynard (2018, 2021) investigated the benefits of keeping a diary for 
university language students’ motivation and L2 confidence. The replication study by 
Spricigo (2023) aimed to confirm original findings within a different educational context.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this request. Throughout the full text (pp. 187, 188, 191, 192, 204), the authors consistently refer in the singular to 'the original study' and 'an original investigation conducted on university students (Shelton-Strong & Mynard, 2018, 2021)', which Table 1 (p. 193) identifies as the confidence-building diary (CBD) study with 39 university language students conducted at the self-access learning center at Kanda University, Japan, in 2018. The 2018 Relay Journal article (shipped row input_row_index 568, DOI 10.37237/relay/010204) and the 2021 Innovation in Language Learning and Teaching article (blind target_index 0, DOI 10.1080/17501229.2020.1825445) are co-cited preliminary and full reports of that same 2018 Kanda University investigation; no separate empirical study or distinct finding from 2018 is tested independently of 2021. Because this single replication-original pair is already represented by shipped row 568, target 0 is not a missing original target.

decisions.quote:
This paper aimed to replicate the general
auditory factor and examined whether and how the hierarchical and faceted Berlin Intelligence Structure model
(BIS; Jäger, 1982) should be extended by adding an auditory dimension.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this request. Only the abstract is available in the source file, and it states that the paper aimed to replicate 'the general auditory factor' while examining whether the Berlin Intelligence Structure model (BIS; Jäger, 1982, shipped row input_row_index 74)—which had yet to include an auditory dimension—should be extended by adding one. Thus, Jäger (1982) is cited for the baseline BIS model being extended rather than as the prior empirical study that established the general auditory factor, and the abstract-only evidence does not identify which published empirical work reporting the general auditory factor is being replicated.
